chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Isma'il al-Anbari, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ali, from Abi al-Maghra', from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:
I heard Aba 'Abdillah (عليه السلام) saying: “Woe to the tyrants of the Arabs from a matter that has drawn near.”
I said: “May I be sacrificed for you, how many of the Arabs will be with al-Qa'im?”
I said: “By Allah, those among them who speak of this matter are surely many.”
He said: “People must inevitably be tested, distinguished, and sifted, and through the sifting many people will be removed.”

key_terms.الْغِرْبَالِ: The sieve; a metaphor for the process of filtering people through trials.
key_terms.الْقَائِمِ: The one who rises; here referring to al-Qa'im from the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
key_terms.طُغَاةِ: Tyrants; those who exceed bounds in oppression and rebellion.
key_terms.وَيْلٌ: A declaration of woe and severe warning.
key_terms.يُغَرْبَلُوا: To be sifted, as grain is sifted through a sieve.
key_terms.يُمَحَّصُوا: To be thoroughly tested and purified through trial.
key_terms.يُمَيَّزُوا: To be distinguished and separated from one another.

ai.seo_question: Why does the hadith say only a small number will remain with al-Qa'im despite many claiming this matter?
ai.summary: This hadith reports from Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) about a near-coming matter that will be severe for the tyrants of the Arabs and states that only a small number of Arabs will be with al-Qa'im. It emphasizes that mere claim or description of the cause is not enough, because people will undergo examination, separation, and sifting until many are filtered out.
